changes.headline: A tanker was involved in an incident with military forces near Chabahar on Sunday
changes.dek: UKMTO report, Sunday Nov 22 evening; vessel, forces and damage all unidentified. A tanker was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman, east of the strait near Chabahar, reported by a company security officer at 14:25 GMT on Sunday (UKMTO, Nov 22). The vessel, the forces involved and any damage or casualties were not identified, and UKMTO said authorities are aware and investigations are ongoing. No United States or CENTCOM statement had been reported in the coverage in hand.
changes.balance_read: The incident is confirmed as an event and unconfirmed in every particular that would make it a supply event: no vessel, no forces, no damage. It reprices transit risk near the blockade line, not barrels, unless verification lands.
changes.publishers: UKMTO, Nov 22, 2026, via euronews and Anadolu

changes.headline: Iran said two supertankers hit mines and caught fire, with no vessel named and no verification
changes.dek: Iranian claim dated Nov 22, unverified; AIS-visible crossings on Nov 22 were 2 ships, 0 tankers. The Revolutionary Guard Navy said two supertankers caught fire after striking naval mines in a restricted area east of the strait, north of Ghanam Island, and one report said one tanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude sank (IRNA via APA, Nov 22). No vessel names, flags or casualty figures were given and the claims have not been independently verified. AIS-visible crossings counted 2 commercial ships on Nov 22, neither of them a tanker, with a seven-day average of 7.3 a day against a pre-crisis 84.8 a day (hormuz.now, Nov 23).
changes.balance_read: A mine claim without a named vessel is a narrative instrument until a second source confirms a hull; the one hard Sunday traffic number, two crossings and no tankers, cuts against the recovery framing rather than for either claim.
changes.vintage: Iranian statement, Nov 22, 2026; crossing count to Nov 23, 07:39 UTC
changes.publishers: IRNA via APA, Nov 22, 2026; hormuz.now, updated Nov 23, 2026

changes.headline: Monday opened flat after an early dip, with the short book at its largest of the year
changes.dek: Brent Jan27 $92.67 and WTI Jan27 $83.57 at 0423 GMT Monday, both near flat after an early dip. Brent Jan27 was $92.67, up $0.10, and WTI Jan27 was $83.57, up $0.16, at 0423 GMT on Monday, after Brent dipped to $91.57 and WTI to $82.63 in an early equity selloff (Reuters, Nov 23). Friday settled Brent $92.57 and WTI $83.41, a third consecutive weekly loss for Brent. Managed money WTI net length is +15,814 contracts as of Nov 17, the lowest of 2026, with the short book at 137,797, the largest of the year (CFTC, released Nov 20).
changes.balance_read: Asia priced neither the incident nor the claim, which says the market is waiting for a measured flow print or a named casualty rather than paying for tempo, and the positioning book, shortest of the year, remains the squeeze risk into a thin week.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Nov 23, 2026; CFTC Commitments of Traders, released Nov 20, 2026

flags.title: December apportionment: Light 24 and Heavy 17 at Kerrobert
flags.detail: December Mainline apportionment (Light 24 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert) is announced for December. The Cromer and Superior points for December were not retrievable in any public source. January WCS paper settled -$21.65 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 20) and the January ARV to TMW spread is +$7.65, orderly, and the balance residual is qualified against that pricing rather than carried as a storage forecast. Trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment percentages as published in the notice itself

flags.title: Sunday incident and mine claim unverified, and the strait gauges stay near half of pre-war
flags.detail: Sunday's confirmed incident near Chabahar and Iran's unverified mine claim both lack a named vessel, and the last measured strait clearance is 8.5 million barrels a day through Nov 16, about 50 percent of pre-war, while AIS-visible crossings fell to 2 ships on Nov 22 with no tankers. Wire lines that Hormuz shipments have returned to pre-war levels are not confirmed by these gauges for the strait itself. Trigger: A named vessel or owner statement on either Sunday item, a fresh measured clearance print, or a confirmed cargo loss or closure

flags.title: North Dakota Pipeline disruption, day ten
flags.detail: The North Dakota Pipeline chloride disruption has curtailed the system since Nov 14 with no restart timeline published, entering its tenth day on Monday. Producers were trucking Bakken crude to Dakota Access delivery points with tanks filling, and force majeure declarations stand at Flint Hills Pine Bend and at MPLX. The refinery receipt suspensions reported are of Bakken crude; no WCS buyer outage has been reported. Trigger: An Enbridge restart notice or a published restart timeline for the North Dakota Pipeline

flags.title: Yanbu on a named threat list
flags.detail: The Houthi military spokesperson warned shipping companies to remove vessels from Saudi Red Sea ports, naming Jeddah, Yanbu, Jazan and King Fahd Industrial Port as potential targets (DeepDraft, Nov 22). Yanbu is the Red Sea outlet of the East-West pipeline and the Gulf system's second-largest loading terminal. Nothing has been hit, nothing has closed and no evacuation order has been issued. Trigger: Any strike on a Saudi Red Sea port, a port closure notice, or a mandatory evacuation order from Saudi port authorities
